text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- A thick coat of dry snow covered much of Croatia's central Adriatic coast and its islands after a freak blizzard, unlike anything seen in the last 20 years.
- Due to stable kuna, car insurance premiums will be cheaper by 3.0 percent from January 1.

- Stocks: After a period of stagnation, most closed the week higher. Two top shares, drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka were 4.4 percent and 7.8 percent up, respectively. They were followed by confectioner Kras and food processor Podravka.
- Analysis: 1997 will be the year of stability and economic growth, with average inflation hovering around 4.0 percent.

- Pliva prepares to cut the face value of its shares from 3,700 to 100 kuna, which is to raise the total number of its shares to some 20 million. Brokers expect the new price of the most lucrative Croatian stock to encourage trade and attract - Pensions will rise by 10 percent from January, PM Zlatko Matesa announced. But pensioners asked for an increase of more than 40 percent.

- Croatian Pure Party of Rights and the emigre Croatian Liberation Movement held a mass for the soul of Ante Pavelic, Croatian WW2 fascist leader, in a Zagreb church. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
